A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ToDRE. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial revisions and restructuring.

before.justification: V1 reports original image/video benchmark evaluations, inference-efficiency measurements, ablations, attention analyses, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark and efficiency results, including additional backbone evaluations and a new pivot-selection ablation.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 and Algorithm 1 replace greedy k-center selection, which minimizes maximum similarity, with max-sum diversification, which minimizes cumulative similarity. V2 also introduces random pivot selection for encoders without a [CLS] token and changes Stage 2 from four candidate pruning layers to a single check at 7L/8. These alter the actual pruning procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight image and four video benchmarks and retain the Video Detail Caption qualitative example. MMBench becoming MMBench-EN is a labeling clarification. The additional backbones do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds DivPrune to the main image comparisons at both LLaVA-NeXT sizes, the video comparisons, and the efficiency comparison. V1 cites DivPrune but does not evaluate it in these comparisons. Adding this directly relevant diversity-based competitor substantially strengthens the comparator set; the previous methods and their stated exclusions remain.

E3.justification: V2 adds evaluation configurations using Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct and InternVL2-8B, beyond LLaVA-NeXT-7B/13B. The reported default threshold changes from 0.03 to 0.10, and candidate pruning layers change from L/2, 5L/8, 6L/8, and 7L/8 to 7L/8 alone. Benchmark splits, sample counts, and metrics remain substantially unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 Supplementary Section 3.1 adds a focused ablation comparing [CLS], random, center, and farthest pivot selection at two retention ratios. The threshold sweep replaces 0.01 with 0.15, and the layer sweep removes the five-candidate configuration including L. Existing stage ablations, decoding-attention analyses, and qualitative cases remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or variability estimates. Both average decoding-attention plots over 100 samples per benchmark. The new random-pivot experiment adds no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Numerous results are replaced, and DivPrune and additional-backbone results are added. Table 1 reports LLaVA-NeXT-7B averages changing from 97.3% to 98.2% at 25% retention and 95.1% to 95.0% at 10%; these accompany revised methods/settings, rather than establishing controlled improvements. Table 2 changes ToDRE's video averages from 105.0%/103.3% to 103.1%/100.9%. FasterVLM's 25%-retention VideoMME entry also changes from 36.9 to 33.8.

T1.justification: Equation 4 substantively changes the mathematical selection objective from maximum similarity to summed similarity; v2 adds a cumulative-update equation and its distance interpretation. The appendix's orthogonality assumptions, independence lemma, redundancy definitions, and covariance proof are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion redefine the claimed selection contribution as max-sum diversification rather than greedy k-center selection. The central claims of complementary diversity/relevance pruning, a training-free two-stage framework, and approximately 2.6-fold acceleration remain. The introduction now states validation across four LVLM configurations.

C2.justification: The layer-selection interpretation reverses: v1 Appendix C.2 argues that single-layer checks are insufficient and favors interleaved checks; v2 Supplementary Section 3.3 favors 7L/8 and attributes early-pruning failures to interrupted cross-modal alignment. V2 also interprets random-pivot results as enabling encoders without [CLS] tokens and removes v1's explicit limitation concerning pruning-related computational overhead.

D1.justification: V2 Algorithm 1 explicitly documents feature normalization and masking selected indices, clarifying implementation of cosine similarity and candidate exclusion. The supplement specifies the added Qwen and InternVL checkpoints, and pruning defaults are revised. Hardware disclosures and benchmark-processing information remain largely unchanged; no implementation-code access information is added.

R1.justification: V2 replaces the Gonzalez k-center citation with Ji et al.'s 'Efficient interactive fuzzy keyword search' citation for max-sum diversification, adds the InternVL 2.0 reference, and explicitly characterizes DivPrune's min-max strategy in the supplement. Most related-work discussion and cited works remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, selection-method exposition, and layer-selection discussion undergo substantial rewriting. The title, author/affiliation block, and section terminology change. Lettered appendices preceding the references become a separately numbered supplementary document following the references.

P2.justification: The document changes from predominantly single-column to two-column layout. V1 Figures 1 and 3 are combined into v2 Figure 1, the framework diagram is redrawn, and backbone and pivot-ablation tables are added. Existing supplementary visualizations are enlarged and relocated. A long supplementary proof equation also extends into the neighboring table area.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important weaknesses in v1's empirical support: it directly compares against the closely related DivPrune and tests portability beyond the LLaVA family through Qwen and InternVL evaluations. The pivot ablation further supports the adaptation to different encoders. These substantially strengthen the competitiveness and generality claims. Removing the overhead limitation and introducing unexplained discrepancies between nominally matching 10% results in Tables 1 and 5, such as MME 1464.4 versus 1469.3, weaken reporting but do not outweigh the stronger validation.
